create.name: Arawana Hayashi
create.bio:
Arawana Hayashi is a meditation teacher, choreographer and performer whose work joins contemplative practice with the arts. She is a senior teacher in Shambhala, where she teaches meditation and dharma art grounded in the view that every person has basic goodness, and she has studied bugaku, the ancient court dance of Japan, since 1977, becoming one of its few lineage holders outside Japan. Earlier in her career she directed an interracial street dance company in Boston, co-directed the dance programme at Naropa University and founded two dance companies in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

At the Presencing Institute, which she helped found with Otto Scharmer and colleagues, she leads the development of Social Presencing Theater, an embodied practice of stillness, simple movement and group awareness that helps people sense what is happening in themselves and in the systems they belong to. She teaches it to individuals, schools, companies and community projects in the Americas, Europe and Asia, both in person and online, and offers an awareness practices course for leaders. Her book on Social Presencing Theater, subtitled The Art of Making a True Move, gives practice instructions and stories from this work and has appeared in several languages.

books.title: Social Presencing Theater: The Art of Making a True Move
books.author: Arawana Hayashi
books.description: An introduction to the embodied group practice she developed at the Presencing Institute, covering its roots, principles and exercises. It includes instructions for beginners and accounts of the practice in schools, companies and social projects.
